title: Identifying an unknown carbonyl compound
stem: An unknown liquid Y has the molecular formula C₃H₆O. Its infrared spectrum and mass spectrum were recorded. The main features are summarised below.

data.caption: Spectroscopic data for compound Y
rows: Absorptions at 2850–3000 cm⁻¹; no broad absorption at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹
Most intense (base) peak at m/z = 43; no significant peak at m/z = 29

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) of Y.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the bonds responsible for the absorptions at 1715 cm⁻¹ and at 2850–3000 cm⁻¹, and state what the absence of an absorption at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ shows.
markscheme: no O–H group present / Y is not an alcohol (or enol)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Deduce the formula of the fragment responsible for the peak at m/z = 43 and the species lost from the molecular ion to form it.
parts.notes: Charge required on the fragment for the first mark.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Two isomers of C₃H₆O contain a C=O bond. Deduce, with a reason, whether Y is propanal or propanone.
markscheme: propanal would give a fragment at m/z = 29 (CHO⁺ / C₂H₅⁺) / loss of CH₃ from propanone gives CH₃CO⁺ at 43 as the base peak
